newsitem.title: USA: Clinton recalls Harriman as elegant, indomitable.
newsitem.headline: Clinton recalls Harriman as elegant, indomitable.

text.p: Praising her as a woman of elegance, wisdom and indomitable will, President Bill Clinton on Thursday led a memorial service for Pamela Harriman, the British-born aristocrat who died in Paris last week as U.S. ambassador to France.

"We gather in tribute to Pamela Harriman, patriot and public servant, American ambassador and citizen of the world ... and for so many of us here, a cherished friend," Clinton told mourners at Washington's National Cathedral.

In eulogising Harriman, Clinton paid tribute to a woman whose life spanned seven and a half decades, two continents and three husbands and took her from her birth into the British aristocracy to a place in the U.S. establishment.
The service included many members of Harriman's family from her first marriage to Randolph Churchill, son of the late British Prime Minister Winston Churchill.

The U.S. establishment was also well represented including Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, historian Arthur Schlesinger and Theodore Sorenson, a top adviser to the late President John F. Kennedy.
Harriman, who was named U.S. ambassador to France in 1993, died at age 76 one week ago after suffering a brain hemmorhage after a regular exercise swim in the Hotel Ritz in Paris.

Her entree to U.S. society and the Democratic Party came through her third marriage, to the late Averell Harriman, a governor of New York, diplomat and major Democratic party figure. After marrying, she became a naturalised U.S. citizen.
She was to be buried alongside him at Arden, the Harriman family estate in upstate New York on Friday.
Her casket was draped in a white cloth with gold cross on entry into the cathedal and an American flag upon departure.

In his eulogy, Clinton recalled Harriman's life as one of remarkable sweep, encompassing the bombing of London during World War II and the 50th anniversary celebration of the D-Day allied invasion of France half a century later.
Clinton, attending the service with wife Hillary, Vice President Al Gore and Tipper Gore, said he and Mrs. Clinton had often talked about what made Harriman remarkable.

"It was more than her elegance, as unforgettable as that was. It was more than the lilt of her voice and her laughter, more even than the luminous presence that could light up a room, a convention hall, or even the city of light itself," Clinton said. "... I think it was, most of all, that she was truly indomitable."

Harriman, once a top Democratic party fund-raiser, devoted some of that indomitable will to helping Clinton win the presidency in 1992. "Today, I am here in no small measure because she was there," he said at the ceremony.
Three members of the Churchill family gave readings: Harriman's son, Winston S. Churchill, who is a Member of the British Parliament, and grandchildren Randolph S. Churchill and Marina S. Churchill.
After her husband's death in 1986, she devoted herself to a cause he would have approved, helping rebuild a Democratic party weakend by years of Republican White House domination.
